images.caption: Figure 1:SLA unifies heterogeneous robot data, aligns intermediate visual embeddings with frozen 3D features during training, and improves benchmark and real-world manipulation performance.

Figure 2:Depth probing of the visual embeddings of VLAs.Embeddings learned solely from 2D images without alignment do not produce meaningful spatial structures. The aligned embeddings inherently contain rich spatial information, leading to better performance in depth probing.

Figure 3:Comparison of rotational action distributions.(a)Euler-angle representations with direct subtraction for relative-rotation targets.(b)Rotation-vector representations with relative rotations computed throughSO⁡(3)\mathrm{SO}(3)composition. In (a), angular wrapping produces outliers near±2​π\pm 2\pi, which widen the interval between the 1st and 99th percentiles. This severely compresses the range of typical action values after normalization, hindering training.

Figure 4:Continual pre-training data scaling ablation.SLA alignment is independently enabled or disabled during continual pre-training and post-training. All curves start at the sharedπ0.5\pi_{0.5}baseline. Experiments are conducted under RoboTwin Clean2Random settings to evaluate success rates (%,↑\uparrow).

Figure 5:Produce manipulation tasks under human perturbations and embodiment changes.A–C conditions share a policy post-trained on 100 demonstrations collected in the A scene configuration, with no additional demonstrations of the perturbations in B or C scene. D condition evaluates a policy jointly post-trained on 100 Piper demonstrations collected in the A scene and 10 Franka demonstrations collected in the D scene.

Figure 6:Tabletop manipulation tasks under changes in object, table height, and instruction target.All four conditions share a policy post-trained on 100 demonstrations collected in the E scene configuration. The bottle, tissue box, pen, and watch are included in these demonstrations while black tape and carrot are excluded.
